question: Using the customary setting of the mathematics used for quantum mechanics, is it possible to prove the existence of Gödelßs god-like entities?

3.text:
The mathematics that is actually used in the textbook formulation of quantum
mechanics is ordinary set-theoretic mathematics. A separable complex
Hilbert space, self-adjoint operators, spectral measures, etc. all live in
ZFC + a little functional analysis. In particular the whole of first order
modal logic S5 and the first order language in which Gödel writes

P(x): x is positive,  G(x): x is God-like, etc.

is definable in that background.  So there is no formal strength
obstruction to writing Gödel’s axioms

* If P is positive and P -> Q is provable then Q is positive,
* Necessity is normal, S5,
* etc.

and the usual modal derivation

Necessarily ∃x G(x) → ∃x G(x) ,  P(G) etc. → ◻∃x G(x)

inside the set theory that underlies the Hilbert space formalism.  In that
strictly formal sense the argument can be reproduced in the same
mathematical universe that is used for QM. The derivation is
conditional on Gödel’s metaphysical axioms about the notion of a
positive property and about the modal logic S5.  It is a proof of
consistency-relative existence in a formal model, not a physical
demonstration of the existence of a real entity.

In particular the argument does not become physically compelling by being
phrased in Hilbert space language.  If the logic that is taken to be
native to quantum mechanics is the non-distributive orthomodular quantum
logic of projections, the classical closure of positive properties that
Gödel uses, and the unrestricted classical conjunction of incompatible
properties that is needed for a single entity to possess all positive
properties at once, fails.  In quantum theory there is in general no
simultaneous eigenstate for incompatible observables; Kochen–Specker type
no-go theorems are the formal expression of that fact.  Hence the
unconditional physical existence of a maximally positive, i.e. 
God-like, entity is not secured by the quantum-mechanical formalism and
the usual Gödel derivation loses its physical content once the classical
modal positivity axioms are required to hold in the quantum-logical
structure.  That is the usual way of saying that Gödel’s proof is a
formal consistency result, not a physical proof of existence.

8.text:
In the customary textbook formulation quantum mechanics is just ordinary
classical mathematics applied to a complex separable Hilbert space.
The physical content is

* H a complex Hilbert space, ||.|| the norm, <.,.> the scalar product,
* observables self-adjoint operators on H, states rays in P(H) or density
operators on H, 
* time evolution unitary, measurement the spectral theorem etc.

All of that is done in the usual background of ZFC + analysis, i.e. in the
same classical first order mathematics in which you can write down any
usual first order proof, in particular a proof in first order modal logic
S5. In that purely formal meta-mathematical sense Gödel's ontological
argument can be written down with the same mathematical resources that
underlie the Hilbert-space formalism.

What is not a theorem of the Hilbert-space formalism is the material
content of Gödel's argument. The argument lives in S5 with a primitive
unary predicate P x meaning "x is a positive property" and the usual
axioms

* P x -> P Nec x
* P x & P y -> P (x & y)
* P x -> ~P ~x
* P G, etc.

and the definition

G x  :=  x possesses every positive property

together with the modal axiom that what is necessarily possible is
necessarily actual for positive properties.  None of those notions -
positivity, necessity/possibility in the metaphysical sense, the axiom
that the property of necessary existence is positive - are mathematical
predicates of a Hilbert space, nor are they consequences of the spectral
theorem, the Schrödinger equation, the C*-algebraic formulation, or of
any other theorem of ordinary quantum mechanics.  They are
metaphysical/ logical premises.

Hence you can reproduce Gödel's derivation in the meta-mathematics that
is the background of the physical formalism, but you do not get a
theorem of quantum mechanics itself, and in particular you do not get
the positivity axioms, and a fortiori the conclusion ∃x G x, from the
customary mathematical physics of Hilbert spaces and operators.  In a
physically meaningful sense the existence of a Gödelian god-like being is
not a consequence of, nor even statable in, the mathematics that is
actually used to do quantum mechanics.  The proof is a modal-logical one,
not a physical one.

6.text:
The formalism that is normally taken for quantum mechanics is the
ordinary mathematical physics of separable complex Hilbert spaces,
self-adjoint operators, spectral measures, etc.  In set theoretic
terms that is just ZFC plus ordinary analysis, in fact a good deal
more than is needed for first order modal logic.  So the argument can
be written down inside that formal language.  That is a purely
syntactic point.

What cannot be obtained from the Hilbert space formalism is the
material content of Gödel’s proof. Gödel’s “God” is defined in modal
logic S5 as the entity which has every positive property and

* P is positive → ¬P is negative,
* if P is positive and P→Q then Q is positive,
* necessarily P is positive → P is positive,
* existence is positive,
* for every positive property P, necessarily P is positive → P.

and the modal axioms

□p → p, □p → □□p, ◊p → □◊p

etc.  The theorem is

∃x Gx → □∃x Gx,    G→ P,
and then □∃x Gx, i.e. necessary existence of a being with all
positive properties.

All of this is a piece of first order modal logic with a non-logical
predicate  Positive .  `Positive’ and `necessary existence’ are not
mathematical notions of the Hilbert space theory of quantum mechanics.
They are metaphysical primitives.  The mathematics of quantum
mechanics gives you no definition of a positive property, no
interpretation of □ as metaphysical necessity, and no justification
for the five Gödelian axioms about positivity and for the S5
principles.  In particular the mathematics of quantum mechanics does
not entail

* Necessarily, if a property is positive then it is necessarily
positive, nor
* Existence is a positive property,

and it does not validate the classical modal logic that Gödel’s
derivation uses, let alone the classical distributive logic that is
replaced in the standard quantum-logical rendering of the theory by
the orthomodular lattice of projections.

Hence within the usual mathematical language of quantum theory the
Gödelian premises are unprovable, and indeed meaningless, extra-
mathematical assumptions. You can formalise the derivation once the
premises are postulated, because ZFC is more than strong enough to
formalise S5, but the existence of a Gödelian god-like entity is not a
theorem of Hilbert-space mathematics. It is a theorem of Gödel’s
modal system plus his ontological axioms, which are not theorems of,
and are not derivable from, the customary mathematics of quantum
mechanics.  In that substantive sense the existence claim cannot be
proved from quantum mechanical mathematics alone.

10.text:
In the ordinary mathematical physics of quantum theory the object language is
the language of ZFC + real/complex analysis + linear algebra over a separable
complex Hilbert space H.  In particular the object language is first order
with the usual Boolean connectives and quantifiers over real vectors,
bounded selfadjoint operators, spectral measures etc. It is the classical
language of set theory and functional analysis in which the theory of
Hilbert spaces can be developed.

Gödel's ontological argument is a theorem of a classical modal logic,
normally S5, with a non logical primitive `P(x)` for *x is positive* and
the axioms

* Positive properties are closed under conjunction, implication and the D
necessity operator.
* If P is positive then necessarily P is positive.
* Existence is positive.
* etc.

and the definition

G := the Godlike being is the individual that has all and only positive
properties.

The theorem is

Necessarily, if G has a positive property then G exists necessarily.

and from the axiom that existence is positive one gets
$\vdash \,\Box\exists x\, G(x)$.

The argument is therefore a purely logical theorem relative to the modal
axioms about positivity.  Those axioms are metaphysical, not analytic,
axioms about the predicate `P`. They are not theorems of the lattice of
closed subspaces of a Hilbert space, nor of the algebra of bounded
operators on H, nor of the usual spectral calculus. The Hilbert-space
formalism is the non-modal, classical language of $L_{\omega\omega}( {\rm
Set})$ with the usual Boolean connectives. The necessity operator
$\Box$, and the second order closure `P` is positive iff ... , are not part
of the customary mathematical language of non-relativistic quantum
mechanics.

What can be done is what can be done in any formal system rich enough to
code syntax, viz. ZFC, which underlies the analysis used in quantum
mechanics.  In the metalanguage one can formalise S5 and Gödel's axioms
inside ZFC and then reproduce Gödel's derivation as a formal derivation in
ZFC.  That is a formalisability statement, not a physical proof.  The
existence of a Godlike being is then existence relative to the acceptance
of Gödel's positivity axioms and to the modal logic S5. The axioms are
undecided and in fact highly controversial in the physical/mathematical
literature, and they are not consequences of the spectral theorem,
Stone-von Neumann theorem, the canonical commutation relations or any
other theorem of the standard Hilbert-space theory of quantum mechanics.

In the usual quantum-logical language the lattice $L(H)$ of closed
subspaces is orthomodular, not Boolean, and has no canonical modal
necessity operator. A modal S5 necessity can be imposed externally, but it
is not generated by the physics. Hence there is no theorem of the
customary quantum-mechanical mathematics that yields
$\exists x\,G(x)$, let alone $\Box\exists x\,G(x)$, without importing the
whole metaphysical modal apparatus by hand. The `proof' is therefore only
a conditional formalisation in the metalanguage of ZFC, not a theorem of
the Hilbert-space/operator-algebra mathematics used in physics proper. ∎

4.text:
In the physics sense no. The formal apparatus that is normally called the
mathematics of quantum mechanics is the Hilbert space apparatus

* a separable complex Hilbert space H ,
* self-adjoint operators on H , spectral measures, unitary time
evolution etc.,

together with the background set theory that makes the Hilbert-space
theory well defined, i.e. essentially ZF + AC and the usual analysis that
goes with it.  That is a language of vectors, inner products, operators,
spectra and probabilities. It has no primitive notion of necessity,
possibility, positive property, essential property and it has no
modal operators at all.

Gödel’s ontological argument is a proof in modal propositional
predicate logic, in the usual presentation S5, with a definite
metaphysical vocabulary

P(x) : x is positive,
Ess(x,P) : P is essential to x,
God(x) : x has every positive property essentially

and axioms such as

1. If P is positive then ¬P is negative,
2. If P is positive then necessarily P is positive,
3. If P is positive and x has P essentially then God has P
essentially,
etc.

The derivation of

∃x God(x)

is a purely logical derivation from those metaphysical premises. It can
be, and routinely is, formalised in the same set theoretic background
that also underlies the Hilbert space formalism, because S5 first order
modal logic is arithmetical and therefore interpretable in ZF. In that
formal-metamathematical sense the argument is expressible in the same
mathematics that you use to write down H, L2(R3), etc.

It is not and cannot be a consequence of the quantum mechanical
Hilbert space formalism itself. The Hilbert space formalism contains no
operators representing “positivity of a property” or “necessary
existence”, and no physical measurement in the theory can be identified
with the evaluation of a modal predicate. The ontological proof therefore
does not follow from quantum theory, it follows only from the
extra-physical modal-metaphysical axioms that are imported into the
background logic. At most you get the trivial statement that the
ontological argument can be written down in the set theory that is also
used to found quantum mechanics; you do not get a physical derivation of
a maximally great being from states, observables and the Born rule.

That is why the argument is usually described as a consistency proof
within a chosen modal logic rather than as a physical existence proof.
∎

13.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: No. The customary mathematics of non-relativistic quantum mechanics is the theory of separable complex Hilbert spaces, self-adjoint operators and, in the algebraic formulation, C*- and von Neumann algebras over ℂ with the usual spectral calculus and the Born rule. This is ordinary classical analysis and set theory, with the logical connectives interpreted classically and with no intrinsic modal structure.

Gödel’s ontological argument is a modal argument in a higher-order quantified modal logic with the S5 necessity operator interpreted over a Kripke frame. Its axioms about positive properties, the concept of God-like as necessarily possessing every positive property, and the modal bridge axioms require a classical possible-worlds semantics with a defined accessibility relation and a classical truth-functional propositional logic.

That semantics cannot be identified with the Hilbert-space formalism without changing the formalism itself. In particular, the quantum-logical propositions of a system are the closed subspaces of a Hilbert space, or the projections in a von Neumann algebra, whose lattice is orthomodular and non-distributive. The modal operator of Gödel’s system has no natural, structure-preserving interpretation as an operator or map on Hilbert space, and adding a Kripke frame of possible worlds to a C*-algebraic model breaks the usual * -representation, the spectral theorem and the probabilistic interpretation that define the customary setting of quantum mechanics. 

Hence the ontological axioms cannot be internalised in the standard mathematical language used for quantum mechanics, and no proof of the existence of a God-like entity can be carried out inside that customary setting.

15.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: No, not in the ordinary ontological sense, and not unconditionally.

The mathematics that is customarily used in non-relativistic quantum theory is ordinary classical mathematics, essentially ZFC set theory plus linear algebra, functional analysis and measure theory over the complex field. In particular it is a formal first-order theory. Gödel’s ontological argument can be expressed in that background theory: the modal language S5 with the usual definitions

P(x) is positive,  E(x) : x exists,  G(x) : x is God-like = ∀P[ P(x) → P(x) ]
and the axioms

A1. P(x) → □P(x)
A2. P(x) ∧ P(y) → P(x∧y)
A3. ¬P(¬P) etc.,

can be formalised in set theory and the derivation

□∃x G(x) → ∃x G(x)

goes through in S5. So the argument is *expressible* in the same formal
system that underlies Hilbert spaces, C*-algebras and spectral theory.

That is all that can be said formally. The derivation is conditional on
the modal positivity axioms A1–A3 and on the S5 logic. Those axioms are
not theorems of ZFC/analysis and they are not supplied by the Hilbert
space formalism of quantum mechanics. A formal ‘∃x G(x)’ obtained in a
model of the axioms is existence-in-that-model, i.e. consistency-relative
existence, not a proof of existence in the physical or metaphysical
world. In particular the Boolean algebra of classical propositions on
which the Gödel proof is built is not the orthomodular lattice of
quantum propositions, and the existence claim is therefore not
derivable from the physics itself.

In the usual metamathematical sense this is exactly the Gödel limitation:
the background mathematics of QM is a sufficiently strong formal system
and mathematics can only establish existence relative to axioms. Unconditional
ontological existence of a Gödel god-like being is not a theorem of the
mathematics used in quantum mechanics, and indeed cannot be. ∎

5.text:
The usual mathematical basis of non-relativistic quantum mechanics is ordinary
classical mathematics, ZFC set theory plus functional analysis over the
complex numbers : separable complex Hilbert spaces, self-adjoint operators,
the spectral theorem, $C^{*}$-algebras, etc.  In that first-order
mathematical language there is no modal operator $\Box ,\Diamond$, nor is
there any primitive notion of a positive property and of maximal positivity.

Gödel’s ontological argument is a derivation in normal modal logic $S5$
from

* $P(x)\to\Box P(x)$ : positive properties are necessarily positive,
* $\neg P(x)\to P(\neg P(x))$ : the negation of a positive property is not positive,
* $P(x)\to P(\exists y\,y=x)$ : existence is positive for a property essentially,
etc.,

together with the definition

God$(x)\equiv \forall P\,[\,P(x)\leftrightarrow P\text{ is positive}\,]$

and the modal axiom $\Box(\phi\to\psi)\to(\Box\phi\to\Box\psi)$ of $S5$.
On those premises, in particular on

$ \Box \forall x\,[{\rm God}(x)\to\exists y\,y=x]\to
\forall x\,[{\rm God}(x)\to \Box\exists y\,y=x] $

one gets in $S5$

$\exists x\,{\rm God}(x)$

and in fact $\Box\exists x\,{\rm God}(x)$.  That is a formal validity of
$S5$ + the positivity axioms.  $S5$ is interpretable in ZFC and hence a
formal transcription of the derivation can be carried out in the set-
theoretic foundation which also underlies the Hilbert-space mathematics of
QM.

What is not carried out is an unconditional theorem of the ZFC–Hilbert-
space theory. The conclusion $\exists x\,{\rm God}(x)$ is a theorem only
conditionally on the philosophical modal axioms about positivity and on the
modal logic $S5$ itself.  Those axioms are not part of, and are not provable
in, the customary first-order mathematical apparatus used in quantum
mechanics.  In particular they are not part of the functional-analytic,
operator-algebraic language in which quantum mechanics is normally
formulated.

Hence in the strict mathematical sense there is no unconditional proof of
the existence of a Gödelian god-like being from the bare mathematics of
quantum mechanics. The best you can get is the familiar relative result:
if the $S5$ positivity axioms are taken as true, then the existence of a
necessary maximally positive entity is a logical consequence, and that
formal derivation can be represented inside the set-theoretic foundation
shared with quantum mechanics. The existence is not a theorem of ZFC or of
the Hilbert-space theory alone.

9.text:
In the mathematical physics literature quantum mechanics is normally formulated
in the ordinary set theoretic classical analysis

* a separable complex Hilbert space H
* self-adjoint operators, spectral measures, C*-algebras etc.

and the logic which is used for the manipulation of that structure is the
usual first order classical logic of ZFC+analysis.  The necessity operator
$\Box$, the second order predicate 

$$ P(x) \hbox{ is positive }$$

and the axioms

A1  $P$ is positive $\rightarrow \Box P$ is positive,
A2  $P$ is positive $\rightarrow \neg P$ is not positive,
A3  Existence is positive,

which are the metaphysical content of Gödel's ontological argument, do not
occur in the physical formalism.  The formalism knows positive operators
in the sense $A\ge0$, spectral projections etc., but it has no notion of a
necessarily positive property of an abstract object and no modal S5
necessity.  In particular the Hilbert space formalism contains no predicate
of positivity of properties and no modal box, so the Gödel system cannot be
stated, let alone proved, inside the physics proper.

Of course the set theory ZFC which is the meta-language in which
Hilbert spaces are defined is strong enough to state the modal second order
theory in which Gödel's argument is a theorem.  Formally the argument can
be reproduced in the metatheory of quantum mechanics and is therefore
syntactically consistent with the mathematics that underlies QM.  That is
only a logical consistency statement.  It is not a physical theorem.  The
existence of a Gödelian God-like entity $\exists x \bigwedge_{P\;{\rm positive}}P(x)$
is the existence of an object satisfying all positive properties under the
modal-metaphysical axioms A1–A3.  Those axioms are not part of, and have
no operational interpretation in, the customary Hilbert-space operator
mathematics of quantum mechanics.  Hence there is no proof of a
Gödelian god-like entity from the physical formalism itself, and any
"proof" is a purely logical, conditional, metaphysical proof in the
set-theoretic metalanguage, with no empirical physical content.  In the
strict physics sense the existence is not proved.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: No. The formal apparatus that is actually customary in quantum mechanics is the usual classical analysis on separable complex Hilbert spaces, operator algebras and spectral theory, all developed in ordinary first-order ZFC with classical propositional and predicate logic. Gödel’s ontological argument is formulated in quantified modal logic S5 with a second-order closure condition on the class of positive properties, and its validity is read off in Kripke semantics for S5.

In the physicists’ mathematical setting there is no primitive modal operator interpreted over a domain of possible worlds, and the intended propositional calculus for quantum propositions is not Boolean at all. The lattice of physical propositions in the standard formalism is the orthomodular lattice of projection operators on a Hilbert space. That lattice is non-distributive, and the necessitation and Barcan rules that drive the S5 derivation of “necessarily positive implies positive” are not validated by the usual state-functional semantics on that lattice. In other words the modal closure conditions Gödel uses have no natural interpretation inside the Hilbert-space / C* -algebra framework that furnishes the customary mathematics of quantum mechanics, so the ontological argument cannot be formalised, let alone proved, within that customary setting.

1.text:
In the ordinary use of the subject the mathematics of quantum mechanics is
just the ordinary classical mathematics of analysis. The state space is a
separable complex Hilbert space H, observables are self-adjoint operators on
H, states are rays, etc. That is ZF + the usual functional analysis, i.e.
classical first order logic with the usual set-theoretic background, and
normally interpreted in a classical metatheory.

Godel’s ontological argument is a derivation in a modal first order logic,
in the usual presentation S5, from a very particular set of metaphysical
axioms about properties, e.g.

* P is positive iff P is not contradictory;
* If P is positive then ¬P is not positive;
* If P is positive then necessarily P is positive;
* If P is positive then necessarily P is positive;
* If P is necessarily positive then the property of necessarily having P is
positive;
* Positive properties are instantiated.

and the definition
G  is the property of possessing all positive properties.

From those premises S5 proves

∃x G(x)      and      □∃x G(x)

The derivation is a purely formal one. It can be formalised in any classical
metatheory able to talk about a modal language, and in particular in the
set theory which underlies the Hilbert space formalism of QM. What it does
not do is derive the positivity/essence axioms from the functional analytic
machinery that describes states, observables and probabilities. Those
axioms are not theorems of ZF, of C*-algebra theory or of the spectral
calculus, and they are not empirical consequences of the quantum formalism.
They are substantial metaphysical premises about the nature of properties and
necessity.

Hence at most one can say that the argument can be encoded in the classical
mathematics that is already being used to do quantum mechanics and, on the
assumption of Godel’s axioms, the formal conditional existence result goes
through. It is not a consequence of the physics, nor is it a physical
existence statement about an entity in H or in the algebra of observables.
In the physical sense the mathematics of quantum mechanics gives no
additional axioms that would establish the Godelian positivity axioms and
so gives no proof of the existence of a God-like entity from physics. The
existence proved is merely the conditional formal existence of a nominal
object satisfying the defined modal property under the stipulated
metaphysical premises. That is the usual status of the Godel ontological
proof, and it is not altered by the Hilbert space setting.

2.text:
In the ordinary textbook formalism the mathematical background of quantum mechanics is classical mathematics: a complex separable Hilbert space $H$, the algebra $B(H)$ of bounded operators on $H$, spectral theory, $C^{*}$–algebras etc., all formulated in the usual set-theoretic foundation,  ZFC, with classical bivalent first order logic.  That is the mathematics that is actually used to make the physical predictions of the theory.

Gödel's ontological argument is a derivation in a modal first order
logic, normally S5, from

* $P(x)$ = '`$x$ has the property $P$' is positive,
* Necessarily $P(x)$ is positive if $P(x)$ is positive,
* Necessarily, $\,P(x)$ implies $\,{\rm Possibly}\,E(x)$ for positive $P$,
etc.

to

$\square\Diamond E(G)\to \square E(G)$  and hence under the usual S5
axioms to $\exists x\,G(x)$ for the property

$G(x)\equiv \forall P\,[P(x)\leftrightarrow {\rm Pos}(P)]$,

i.e. a being that has all and only positive properties.  The
derivation is a purely logical one. It can be coded up in ZFC by
coding a Kripke frame as a set and the modal operators as
quantification over the frame, so that the formal statement

$${\rm S5}+{\rm PosAx}\vdash \exists x\,G(x)$$

is a theorem of ordinary set theory and therefore can be written down
in the same set-theoretic background that underlies functional analysis.

That formal availability is all that is obtained.  The proof uses no
Hilbert-space structure, no operator algebra, no non-commutativity,
no superposition etc., at all. It uses a substantive metaphysical
definition of ‘positive property’ and the modal axioms of S5, i.e. the
identification of metaphysical necessity with truth in all accessible
worlds.  The consequent $\exists x\,G(x)$ is therefore a formal
existence claim in the model theory of S5, not an empirical claim
about physical states of affairs.  In particular it gives no observable,
operational content in the Hilbert space formalism, and it does not
become any more or less true because the state space is a complex
Hilbert space rather than a real one.  In the physically relevant
sense there is no quantum-mechanical proof of a maximally great being;
the Gödel derivation, if at all accepted, is a purely logical-metaphysical
one that can be written down in the same classical mathematics that
happens to be used for quantum mechanics, but it adds nothing to the
mathematics of quantum mechanics itself.

11.text:
The mathematics which is actually used in the physics of quantum mechanics is the
ordinary classical mathematics of sets, complex numbers, Hilbert spaces,
self-adjoint operators and spectral theory.  In set-theoretic terms that is
ZFC + analysis.  In that meta-theory modal first order logic S5, and hence
Gödel’s ontological argument, can be formalised.  In that purely formal
sense the derivation can be reproduced. 

What cannot be reproduced is a physical, i.e. Hilbert-space, justification
of the premises.  Gödel’s argument is a conditional theorem of modal
logic:

* P is positive iff …
* If P is positive then Nec P → P etc.
* God is the being that has all positive properties necessarily.

From the axioms of positivity the S5 theorem ∃x Nec φ(x) with φ the
definition of a God-like being follows.  The axioms are metaphysical
axioms about the notion of positivity, about the interaction of
necessity with essence and with positive properties.  They are not
theorems of functional analysis, of the theory of self-adjoint operators,
nor of the projection lattice of a Hilbert space, and they are not
justified by any measurement postulate of quantum mechanics.

In the physically intended reading the properties of a quantum system
are represented by the orthomodular lattice L(H) of projections.  L(H)
is not Boolean, it is only orthomodular, i.e. the distributive law which
is used essentially in the classical modal rendering of Gödel’s axioms
fails.  That is the usual quantum logic of Birkhoff-von Neumann.  On the
quantum logical reading the positive-property closure and the Nec → 
steps of Gödel’s proof are not valid in general, and the ontological
argument is not a theorem of the logic that is intrinsic to the
customary Hilbert space formalism.  In the ordinary physical sense the
argument is therefore an ungrounded conditional.  Mathematics can
establish formal consistency with the axioms, it cannot turn the
uncontrollable metaphysical axioms of positivity and necessary existence
into a physical existence theorem for a God-like entity.  This is the
usual sense in which a physical theory proves existence only of
mathematical models, not of metaphysical entities.

14.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: No. In the customary mathematical setting of non-relativistic quantum mechanics — separable complex Hilbert spaces H, self-adjoint operators on H, spectral measures, C*- and von Neumann algebras, and the usual set-theoretic background for functional analysis — there is no modal apparatus internal to the formalism.

Gödel’s ontological argument is a theorem of a quantified modal logic, essentially S5 with the axiom Possibly necessarily P → necessarily P and the five axioms about the God-like property G, e.g. □(G → P) → P. Its validity is established semantically by Kripke models with an accessibility relation that is an equivalence relation on a set of possible worlds.

Kripke semantics is a set-theoretic semantics for modal logic, not a piece of Hilbert-space mathematics. The operators □ and ◇ have no canonical interpretation as bounded or unbounded operators on a Hilbert space, nor as elements of a C*-algebra, and the “possible worlds” of a Kripke frame are not vectors, rays, or projection lattices in the quantum formalism. The physical mathematics is first-order/second-order analysis over C, with the usual classical propositional connectives. 

Hence within the mathematics actually used to formulate and compute quantum mechanical predictions — functional analysis over complex Hilbert spaces and the standard measure-theoretic apparatus — the modal axioms required for Gödel’s God-like entities are not expressible, let alone provable. A Kripke soundness argument lives in meta-mathematics, not in the operator-algebraic language of quantum theory, so existence cannot be proved in the customary quantum-mechanical setting itself.

12.text:
In the practice of physics the "mathematics of quantum mechanics" is still the
ordinary classical mathematics of sets, of real and complex analysis and of
Hilbert spaces over $\mathbf C$.  The Hilbert–space formalism is defined in
ZFC and the reasoning about it is carried out in the ordinary classical
first order meta–logic.  In particular the usual classical propositional
calculus, first order logic and the normal modal system S5 are all available
in that background.

Gödel’s ontological argument is a theorem

* $P$ positive $\to \Box P$
* $\neg P$ positive $\to \neg P$ is not positive
* $E$ is positive
* $P$ positive $\to \Diamond\exists x\,P(x)$

etc.,

of classical first order modal logic S5.  It is a purely formal theorem of
S5+ first order set theory.  The fact that a proposition $P$ is represented
in the physical theory by a closed subspace of a Hilbert space, or by a
projection operator on that space, does not change the meta-logic in
which the axioms of the ontological argument are stated and proved.  On the
classical set-theoretic background that is already used to define
$\ell^{2}$, $L^{2}(\mathbf R^{3})$, bounded self-adjoint operators, the
spectral theorem, etc., the S5 derivation of

$$\exists x\, \bigwedge_{P\;{\rm positive}} P(x) $$

i.e. the existence of a God-like, necessarily maximally great being, goes
through exactly as in Gödel’s 1970 exposition.  In this ordinary
physicist’s sense the proof is available and is completely independent of
any particular physical content of quantum theory.

Remark.  If the argument is required to be carried out inside the
intrinsic propositional calculus of the theory, i.e. inside the
orthomodular lattice ${\cal L}({\cal H})$ of closed subspaces/projections
of a Hilbert space, then the situation changes.  ${\cal L}({\cal H})$ is
non-distributive and the classical S5 modal axioms which Gödel uses are not
valid for quantum propositions.  In the strict quantum-logical semantics the
usual S5 derivation ceases to be a derivation of physically meaningful
quantum propositions.  That is the only sense in which quantum mechanics
can be said to block the argument.

The mathematics that is actually used in the textbook formulation of quantum
mechanics is ordinary set-theoretic mathematics. A separable complex
Hilbert space, self-adjoint operators, spectral measures, etc. all live in
ZFC + a little functional analysis. In particular the whole of first order
modal logic S5 and the first order language in which Gödel writes

P(x): x is positive,  G(x): x is God-like, etc.

is definable in that background.  So there is no formal strength
obstruction to writing Gödel’s axioms

* If P is positive and P -> Q is provable then Q is positive,
* Necessity is normal, S5,
* etc.

and the usual modal derivation

Necessarily ∃x G(x) → ∃x G(x) ,  P(G) etc. → ◻∃x G(x)

inside the set theory that underlies the Hilbert space formalism.  In that
strictly formal sense the argument can be reproduced in the same
mathematical universe that is used for QM. The derivation is
conditional on Gödel’s metaphysical axioms about the notion of a
positive property and about the modal logic S5.  It is a proof of
consistency-relative existence in a formal model, not a physical
demonstration of the existence of a real entity.

In particular the argument does not become physically compelling by being
phrased in Hilbert space language.  If the logic that is taken to be
native to quantum mechanics is the non-distributive orthomodular quantum
logic of projections, the classical closure of positive properties that
Gödel uses, and the unrestricted classical conjunction of incompatible
properties that is needed for a single entity to possess all positive
properties at once, fails.  In quantum theory there is in general no
simultaneous eigenstate for incompatible observables; Kochen–Specker type
no-go theorems are the formal expression of that fact.  Hence the
unconditional physical existence of a maximally positive, i.e. 
God-like, entity is not secured by the quantum-mechanical formalism and
the usual Gödel derivation loses its physical content once the classical
modal positivity axioms are required to hold in the quantum-logical
structure.  That is the usual way of saying that Gödel’s proof is a
formal consistency result, not a physical proof of existence.

In the customary textbook formulation quantum mechanics is just ordinary
classical mathematics applied to a complex separable Hilbert space.
The physical content is

* H a complex Hilbert space, ||.|| the norm, <.,.> the scalar product,
* observables self-adjoint operators on H, states rays in P(H) or density
operators on H, 
* time evolution unitary, measurement the spectral theorem etc.

All of that is done in the usual background of ZFC + analysis, i.e. in the
same classical first order mathematics in which you can write down any
usual first order proof, in particular a proof in first order modal logic
S5. In that purely formal meta-mathematical sense Gödel's ontological
argument can be written down with the same mathematical resources that
underlie the Hilbert-space formalism.

What is not a theorem of the Hilbert-space formalism is the material
content of Gödel's argument. The argument lives in S5 with a primitive
unary predicate P x meaning "x is a positive property" and the usual
axioms

* P x -> P Nec x
* P x & P y -> P (x & y)
* P x -> ~P ~x
* P G, etc.

and the definition

G x  :=  x possesses every positive property

together with the modal axiom that what is necessarily possible is
necessarily actual for positive properties.  None of those notions -
positivity, necessity/possibility in the metaphysical sense, the axiom
that the property of necessary existence is positive - are mathematical
predicates of a Hilbert space, nor are they consequences of the spectral
theorem, the Schrödinger equation, the C*-algebraic formulation, or of
any other theorem of ordinary quantum mechanics.  They are
metaphysical/ logical premises.

Hence you can reproduce Gödel's derivation in the meta-mathematics that
is the background of the physical formalism, but you do not get a
theorem of quantum mechanics itself, and in particular you do not get
the positivity axioms, and a fortiori the conclusion ∃x G x, from the
customary mathematical physics of Hilbert spaces and operators.  In a
physically meaningful sense the existence of a Gödelian god-like being is
not a consequence of, nor even statable in, the mathematics that is
actually used to do quantum mechanics.  The proof is a modal-logical one,
not a physical one.

The formalism that is normally taken for quantum mechanics is the
ordinary mathematical physics of separable complex Hilbert spaces,
self-adjoint operators, spectral measures, etc.  In set theoretic
terms that is just ZFC plus ordinary analysis, in fact a good deal
more than is needed for first order modal logic.  So the argument can
be written down inside that formal language.  That is a purely
syntactic point.

What cannot be obtained from the Hilbert space formalism is the
material content of Gödel’s proof. Gödel’s “God” is defined in modal
logic S5 as the entity which has every positive property and

* P is positive → ¬P is negative,
* if P is positive and P→Q then Q is positive,
* necessarily P is positive → P is positive,
* existence is positive,
* for every positive property P, necessarily P is positive → P.

and the modal axioms

□p → p, □p → □□p, ◊p → □◊p

etc.  The theorem is

∃x Gx → □∃x Gx,    G→ P,
and then □∃x Gx, i.e. necessary existence of a being with all
positive properties.

All of this is a piece of first order modal logic with a non-logical
predicate  Positive .  `Positive’ and `necessary existence’ are not
mathematical notions of the Hilbert space theory of quantum mechanics.
They are metaphysical primitives.  The mathematics of quantum
mechanics gives you no definition of a positive property, no
interpretation of □ as metaphysical necessity, and no justification
for the five Gödelian axioms about positivity and for the S5
principles.  In particular the mathematics of quantum mechanics does
not entail

* Necessarily, if a property is positive then it is necessarily
positive, nor
* Existence is a positive property,

and it does not validate the classical modal logic that Gödel’s
derivation uses, let alone the classical distributive logic that is
replaced in the standard quantum-logical rendering of the theory by
the orthomodular lattice of projections.

Hence within the usual mathematical language of quantum theory the
Gödelian premises are unprovable, and indeed meaningless, extra-
mathematical assumptions. You can formalise the derivation once the
premises are postulated, because ZFC is more than strong enough to
formalise S5, but the existence of a Gödelian god-like entity is not a
theorem of Hilbert-space mathematics. It is a theorem of Gödel’s
modal system plus his ontological axioms, which are not theorems of,
and are not derivable from, the customary mathematics of quantum
mechanics.  In that substantive sense the existence claim cannot be
proved from quantum mechanical mathematics alone.

In the ordinary mathematical physics of quantum theory the object language is
the language of ZFC + real/complex analysis + linear algebra over a separable
complex Hilbert space H.  In particular the object language is first order
with the usual Boolean connectives and quantifiers over real vectors,
bounded selfadjoint operators, spectral measures etc. It is the classical
language of set theory and functional analysis in which the theory of
Hilbert spaces can be developed.

Gödel's ontological argument is a theorem of a classical modal logic,
normally S5, with a non logical primitive `P(x)` for *x is positive* and
the axioms

* Positive properties are closed under conjunction, implication and the D
necessity operator.
* If P is positive then necessarily P is positive.
* Existence is positive.
* etc.

and the definition

G := the Godlike being is the individual that has all and only positive
properties.

The theorem is

Necessarily, if G has a positive property then G exists necessarily.

and from the axiom that existence is positive one gets
$\vdash \,\Box\exists x\, G(x)$.

The argument is therefore a purely logical theorem relative to the modal
axioms about positivity.  Those axioms are metaphysical, not analytic,
axioms about the predicate `P`. They are not theorems of the lattice of
closed subspaces of a Hilbert space, nor of the algebra of bounded
operators on H, nor of the usual spectral calculus. The Hilbert-space
formalism is the non-modal, classical language of $L_{\omega\omega}( {\rm
Set})$ with the usual Boolean connectives. The necessity operator
$\Box$, and the second order closure `P` is positive iff ... , are not part
of the customary mathematical language of non-relativistic quantum
mechanics.

What can be done is what can be done in any formal system rich enough to
code syntax, viz. ZFC, which underlies the analysis used in quantum
mechanics.  In the metalanguage one can formalise S5 and Gödel's axioms
inside ZFC and then reproduce Gödel's derivation as a formal derivation in
ZFC.  That is a formalisability statement, not a physical proof.  The
existence of a Godlike being is then existence relative to the acceptance
of Gödel's positivity axioms and to the modal logic S5. The axioms are
undecided and in fact highly controversial in the physical/mathematical
literature, and they are not consequences of the spectral theorem,
Stone-von Neumann theorem, the canonical commutation relations or any
other theorem of the standard Hilbert-space theory of quantum mechanics.

In the usual quantum-logical language the lattice $L(H)$ of closed
subspaces is orthomodular, not Boolean, and has no canonical modal
necessity operator. A modal S5 necessity can be imposed externally, but it
is not generated by the physics. Hence there is no theorem of the
customary quantum-mechanical mathematics that yields
$\exists x\,G(x)$, let alone $\Box\exists x\,G(x)$, without importing the
whole metaphysical modal apparatus by hand. The `proof' is therefore only
a conditional formalisation in the metalanguage of ZFC, not a theorem of
the Hilbert-space/operator-algebra mathematics used in physics proper. ∎

This is ordinary classical analysis and set theory, with the logical connectives interpreted classically and with no intrinsic modal structure.

Gödel’s ontological argument is a modal argument in a higher-order quantified modal logic with the S5 necessity operator interpreted over a Kripke frame. Its axioms about positive properties, the concept of God-like as necessarily possessing every positive property, and the modal bridge axioms require a classical possible-worlds semantics with a defined accessibility relation and a classical truth-functional propositional logic.

That semantics cannot be identified with the Hilbert-space formalism without changing the formalism itself. In particular, the quantum-logical propositions of a system are the closed subspaces of a Hilbert space, or the projections in a von Neumann algebra, whose lattice is orthomodular and non-distributive. The modal operator of Gödel’s system has no natural, structure-preserving interpretation as an operator or map on Hilbert space, and adding a Kripke frame of possible worlds to a C*-algebraic model breaks the usual * -representation, the spectral theorem and the probabilistic interpretation that define the customary setting of quantum mechanics. 

Hence the ontological axioms cannot be internalised in the standard mathematical language used for quantum mechanics, and no proof of the existence of a God-like entity can be carried out inside that customary setting.

The mathematics that is customarily used in non-relativistic quantum theory is ordinary classical mathematics, essentially ZFC set theory plus linear algebra, functional analysis and measure theory over the complex field. In particular it is a formal first-order theory. Gödel’s ontological argument can be expressed in that background theory: the modal language S5 with the usual definitions

P(x) is positive,  E(x) : x exists,  G(x) : x is God-like = ∀P[ P(x) → P(x) ]
and the axioms

A1. P(x) → □P(x)
A2. P(x) ∧ P(y) → P(x∧y)
A3. ¬P(¬P) etc.,

can be formalised in set theory and the derivation

□∃x G(x) → ∃x G(x)

goes through in S5. So the argument is *expressible* in the same formal
system that underlies Hilbert spaces, C*-algebras and spectral theory.

That is all that can be said formally. The derivation is conditional on
the modal positivity axioms A1–A3 and on the S5 logic. Those axioms are
not theorems of ZFC/analysis and they are not supplied by the Hilbert
space formalism of quantum mechanics. A formal ‘∃x G(x)’ obtained in a
model of the axioms is existence-in-that-model, i.e. consistency-relative
existence, not a proof of existence in the physical or metaphysical
world. In particular the Boolean algebra of classical propositions on
which the Gödel proof is built is not the orthomodular lattice of
quantum propositions, and the existence claim is therefore not
derivable from the physics itself.

In the usual metamathematical sense this is exactly the Gödel limitation:
the background mathematics of QM is a sufficiently strong formal system
and mathematics can only establish existence relative to axioms. Unconditional
ontological existence of a Gödel god-like being is not a theorem of the
mathematics used in quantum mechanics, and indeed cannot be. ∎

The usual mathematical basis of non-relativistic quantum mechanics is ordinary
classical mathematics, ZFC set theory plus functional analysis over the
complex numbers : separable complex Hilbert spaces, self-adjoint operators,
the spectral theorem, $C^{*}$-algebras, etc.  In that first-order
mathematical language there is no modal operator $\Box ,\Diamond$, nor is
there any primitive notion of a positive property and of maximal positivity.

Gödel’s ontological argument is a derivation in normal modal logic $S5$
from

* $P(x)\to\Box P(x)$ : positive properties are necessarily positive,
* $\neg P(x)\to P(\neg P(x))$ : the negation of a positive property is not positive,
* $P(x)\to P(\exists y\,y=x)$ : existence is positive for a property essentially,
etc.,

together with the definition

God$(x)\equiv \forall P\,[\,P(x)\leftrightarrow P\text{ is positive}\,]$

and the modal axiom $\Box(\phi\to\psi)\to(\Box\phi\to\Box\psi)$ of $S5$.
On those premises, in particular on

$ \Box \forall x\,[{\rm God}(x)\to\exists y\,y=x]\to
\forall x\,[{\rm God}(x)\to \Box\exists y\,y=x] $

one gets in $S5$

$\exists x\,{\rm God}(x)$

and in fact $\Box\exists x\,{\rm God}(x)$.  That is a formal validity of
$S5$ + the positivity axioms.  $S5$ is interpretable in ZFC and hence a
formal transcription of the derivation can be carried out in the set-
theoretic foundation which also underlies the Hilbert-space mathematics of
QM.

What is not carried out is an unconditional theorem of the ZFC–Hilbert-
space theory. The conclusion $\exists x\,{\rm God}(x)$ is a theorem only
conditionally on the philosophical modal axioms about positivity and on the
modal logic $S5$ itself.  Those axioms are not part of, and are not provable
in, the customary first-order mathematical apparatus used in quantum
mechanics.  In particular they are not part of the functional-analytic,
operator-algebraic language in which quantum mechanics is normally
formulated.

Hence in the strict mathematical sense there is no unconditional proof of
the existence of a Gödelian god-like being from the bare mathematics of
quantum mechanics. The best you can get is the familiar relative result:
if the $S5$ positivity axioms are taken as true, then the existence of a
necessary maximally positive entity is a logical consequence, and that
formal derivation can be represented inside the set-theoretic foundation
shared with quantum mechanics. The existence is not a theorem of ZFC or of
the Hilbert-space theory alone.

* If P is positive then necessarily P is positive;
* If P is positive then necessarily P is positive;

and the definition

∃x G(x)      and      □∃x G(x)

necessity.

* Necessarily $P(x)$ is positive if $P(x)$ is positive,
* Necessarily, $\,P(x)$ implies $\,{\rm Possibly}\,E(x)$ for positive $P$,

to

axioms to $\exists x\,G(x)$ for the property

the Gödel derivation, if at all accepted, is a purely logical-metaphysical

happens to be used for quantum mechanics, but it adds nothing to the

ZFC and the reasoning about it is carried out in the ordinary classical
first order meta–logic.  In particular the usual classical propositional
calculus, first order logic and the normal modal system S5 are all available
in that background.

Gödel’s ontological argument is a theorem

* $P$ positive $\to \Box P$
* $\neg P$ positive $\to \neg P$ is not positive
* $E$ is positive
* $P$ positive $\to \Diamond\exists x\,P(x)$

etc.,

of classical first order modal logic S5.  It is a purely formal theorem of
S5+ first order set theory.  The fact that a proposition $P$ is represented
in the physical theory by a closed subspace of a Hilbert space, or by a
projection operator on that space, does not change the meta-logic in
which the axioms of the ontological argument are stated and proved.  On the
classical set-theoretic background that is already used to define
$\ell^{2}$, $L^{2}(\mathbf R^{3})$, bounded self-adjoint operators, the
spectral theorem, etc., the S5 derivation of

$$\exists x\, \bigwedge_{P\;{\rm positive}} P(x) $$

i.e. the existence of a God-like, necessarily maximally great being, goes
through exactly as in Gödel’s 1970 exposition.  In this ordinary
physicist’s sense the proof is available and is completely independent of
any particular physical content of quantum theory.

Remark.  If the argument is required to be carried out inside the
intrinsic propositional calculus of the theory, i.e. inside the
orthomodular lattice ${\cal L}({\cal H})$ of closed subspaces/projections
of a Hilbert space, then the situation changes.  ${\cal L}({\cal H})$ is
non-distributive and the classical S5 modal axioms which Gödel uses are not
valid for quantum propositions.  In the strict quantum-logical semantics the
usual S5 derivation ceases to be a derivation of physically meaningful
quantum propositions.  That is the only sense in which quantum mechanics
can be said to block the argument.

reflection_text.10:

* P positive → □P positive
* existence is positive, etc.
* God-like G := possesses all positive properties necessarily
Theorem: S5+PosAx ⊢ □∃x G(x), hence ∃x G(x).

1.text:
In the mathematical physics sense the "mathematics of quantum mechanics" is
ordinary classical mathematics.  A separable complex Hilbert space $H$, self-
adjoint observables, spectral measures, $C^{*}$- and von Neumann algebras,
the Born rule, etc. are all developed in ZFC + analysis with classical first
order logic in the meta-language.  In that meta-language $S5$ and Gödel's
positivity axioms are arithmetical and therefore formalisable in ZFC.  In
the purely syntactic sense the Gödel derivation

$${\rm PosAx}+S5\vdash \exists x\,G(x),\qquad G(x)\equiv\forall P\bigl[{\rm Pos}(P)\to P(x)\bigr]$$

can be written down in the same set-theoretic background that underlies the
Hilbert-space formalism.  That is a formalisability/consistency statement,
not a physical theorem.

The derivation is conditional on metaphysical premises that are not part of
the customary quantum-mechanical formalism.  The Hilbert-space formalism
has no primitive necessity operator $\Box$, no primitive notion of a
positive property, of essential property, and of necessary existence, and
nothing in spectral theory, the CCR, the Stone–von Neumann theorem or the
Born rule supplies the Gödel axioms

* ${\rm Pos}(P)\to\Box{\rm Pos}(P)$,
* ${\rm Pos}(P)\to {\rm Pos}(\Box P)$,
* existence is positive,
* closure of ${\rm Pos}$ under conjunction/implication,

nor the $S5$ necessitation and iteration principles.  The conclusion
$\Box\exists x G(x)$ is existence-in-a-model of $S5+{\rm PosAx}$, i.e.
consistency-relative existence, with no operational content in $H$ or in
the algebra of observables.

On the intrinsic, quantum-logical reading the situation is stronger.
The physically intended propositional calculus is the orthomodular lattice
${\cal L}(H)$ of closed subspaces/projections, not a Boolean algebra.  The
classical distributive conjunction used in the closure of positive
properties and the unrestricted $S5$ modal steps are not valid in
${\cal L}(H)$ in general; $\Box$ has no canonical structure-preserving
interpretation as an operator or map on $H$.  Imposing $S5$ externally
breaks the $*$–representation and spectral interpretation that define the
customary setting.

Hence there is no unconditional theorem $\exists x G(x)$ of the Hilbert-
space/$C^{*}$-algebraic mathematics used for quantum mechanics, and no
physical existence statement about an entity in $H$ or in the algebra of
observables follows from quantum theory.  At most one obtains the familiar
conditional meta-mathematical fact that, assuming Gödel's modal positivity
axioms, the existence claim is a theorem of the classical set theory in
which quantum mechanics is formulated.  In the physical, intrinsic sense
the existence of a Gödelian god-like entity is not provable from the
customary mathematics of quantum mechanics.

4.text:
In the ordinary textbook use of “the mathematics of quantum mechanics’’ the object language is
classical. The state space is a separable complex Hilbert space H, observables are the
self-adjoint operators on H, states are rays/density operators, time evolution is
unitary, measurement is spectral theory. All of that is developed in ZFC + analysis
with classical first order logic as meta-logic. That is the mathematics actually used
for physical predictions.

Gödel’s ontological argument is a quantified modal S5 argument in a language with a
non-logical primitive Positive(P) and the definition

G(x) ≡ x has all positive properties necessarily,

together with the usual positivity axioms

* Positive is closed under conjunction/implication,
* If P is positive then □P is positive,
* Existence is positive,
* □∃x G(x) → ∃x G(x),

and the S5 necessitation rules. From those premises S5 proves

⊢ □∃x G(x)   and hence ⊢ ∃x G(x).

The derivation is purely modal-logical. ZFC is strong enough to code syntax,
Kripke frames and S5, so in the set-theoretic metalanguage that underlies H,
B(H), C*- and von Neumann algebras the whole derivation can be transcribed.
That is the formalisability point made by Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,10,11,12. Formally
the argument can be written down in the same background that defines ℓ²,
L²(R³), the spectral theorem etc. In that purely syntactic sense the argument
is available.

It is not available physically or internally. □, ◇, Positive(P), Essence and
the S5 closure conditions are not part of the functional-analytic language of
QM. They have no canonical interpretation as bounded/unbounded operators on H,
as spectral measures or as elements of a C*-algebra, and they are not
consequences of the Born rule, the Schrödinger equation or the Stone–von Neumann
theorem. The positivity axioms are metaphysical, not analytic, and they are
undecided in ZFC/analysis.

If the argument is required to be internal to the propositional calculus that is
native to the Hilbert-space formalism the obstruction is sharper. The physical
propositions are the orthomodular lattice L(H) of closed subspaces/projections.
L(H) is non-distributive and has no canonical Boolean modal necessitation.
Gödel’s closure of positive properties under classical conjunction and the S5
necessity-closure are not valid in L(H) in general; Kochen–Specker type
incompatibility blocks the simultaneous possession of all positive properties
that the definition of G demands. That is the quantum-logical reading noted by
Colleagues 11,12,3,7.

Hence the best that can be said is a conditional consistency statement in the
classical metalanguage: if Gödel’s S5 positivity axioms are accepted as extra-
mathematical premises, then ∃x G(x) is a theorem of S5+PosAx and can be
formalised in ZFC. It is not a theorem of the Hilbert-space/operator-algebra
mathematics of quantum mechanics itself, nor is it a physical existence claim
about an entity in H or in the algebra of observables. In the customary
mathematical-physical sense the existence of a Gödel god-like entity is not proved
by quantum mechanics. ∎

formalism is the orthomodular lattice $L(H)$ of closed subspaces / projections.
It has no primitive modal operator $\Box,\Diamond$, no primitive notion of a
positive property in the metaphysical sense, no notion of essential property
and no Kripke accessibility relation.

Gödel's ontological argument is a theorem of quantified modal logic, normally
S5, with a non-logical predicate $Pos(P)$ and the axioms

* $Pos(P)\rightarrow\Box Pos(P)$,
* $Pos(P)\land Pos(Q)\rightarrow Pos(P\land Q)$,
* $\neg Pos(P)\rightarrow\neg Pos(\neg P)$,
* $Pos(Ex)$,
* $Pos(P)\rightarrow Pos(\Box P)$,

and the definition

$G(x)\equiv\forall P\,[Pos(P)\rightarrow P(x)]$,
i.e. $x$ has all positive properties necessarily.

From those premises S5 gives $\vdash\Box\exists x\,G(x)$ and hence
$\exists x\,G(x)$. The derivation is a purely formal logical theorem relative
to the positivity axioms and to S5.

ZFC, which is the background in which $H$, $B(H)$ and the spectral theorem are
defined, is strong enough to code syntax, Kripke frames and S5. Hence the
whole derivation can be transcribed in the metalanguage that underlies the
Hilbert-space formalism. That is a formalisability statement.

It is not a theorem of the Hilbert-space/operator-algebra mathematics itself.
The positivity axioms, the modal axioms of S5 and the identification of
metaphysical necessity with $\Box$ are not theorems of functional analysis,
C*-algebra theory, the spectral calculus, Stone-von Neumann etc., nor are
they empirical consequences of quantum mechanics. $Pos$, $\Box$ and
Essence have no canonical interpretation as operators or maps on $H$ and no
operational content in the Born rule. In the physically intended reading the
propositions of the theory form the orthomodular lattice $L(H)$, which is
non-Boolean and non-distributive, so the classical closure of positive
properties used by Gödel and the unrestricted classical conjunction of
incompatible properties required for a single entity to have all positive
properties at once are not valid on the intrinsic quantum logic. Kochen-Specker
type obstructions are the formal expression of this.

Hence at most one can say that Gödel's conditional theorem can be encoded in
the classical set-theoretic metalanguage that is shared with quantum
mechanics. There is no unconditional, physically meaningful theorem
$\exists x\,G(x)$ derivable from the customary mathematical language of
quantum mechanics, and a fortiori no proof of the existence of a Gödelian
god-like entity from states, observables and the usual quantum formalism.
The existence that is proved is existence in a model of the modal positivity
axioms, not existence in $H$ or in the algebra of observables. In the
physics sense the argument is ungrounded.

The mathematics that is actually customary in non-relativistic quantum mechanics is the object language of separable complex Hilbert spaces, self-adjoint operators, spectral measures, C*- and von Neumann algebras, and the Born rule, developed in ordinary ZFC + analysis. That language has first-order quantifiers over vectors, operators and real numbers, and the usual Boolean connectives. It has no primitive □/◇, no predicate “P is positive in Gödel’s sense”, no notion of essence, and no Kripke frame of possible worlds built into the formalism.

Gödel’s argument is a theorem of quantified modal logic S5 with a non-logical predicate Pos and the axioms about positivity, essentiality and necessary existence. Its soundness is read off in Kripke semantics. A Kripke frame is a set-theoretic object, yes, and S5 can be formalised in ZFC, so in the metalanguage one can code the syntax of S5 and reproduce the derivation inside ZFC. That is a formalisability claim, not a theorem of the Hilbert-space/operator-algebra theory itself.

What is missing is any internal interpretation of the modal apparatus in the customary QM mathematics. □ is not a bounded or unbounded operator on H, it is not a map on the projection lattice L(H), and “possible world” is not a ray, not a density operator, not a state on a C*-algebra. You can import a Boolean modal structure by hand in the metatheory, but that import is extra-physical.

Those axioms are not theorems of ZF, of C*-algebra theory, of the spectral theorem, Stone-von Neumann, or any empirical postulate of quantum mechanics. Hence there is no proof of a God-like entity within the customary mathematical language used to formulate and compute quantum mechanical predictions. The existence is relative to the imported metaphysical modal axioms, not a result of the Hilbert-space mathematics proper.

The mathematics that is actually used to do predictions in non-relativistic quantum mechanics is the Hilbert-space / operator-algebra language: a separable complex Hilbert space H, self-adjoint operators on H, spectral measures, C*- and von Neumann algebras over C, the Born rule, etc. The logical connectives that are used in that language are the ordinary classical first-order connectives interpreted in the set-theoretic background in which H is defined. It has no primitive modal operator, no primitive notion of a positive property in Gödel’s metaphysical sense, and no canonical interpretation of □ or ◇ as an operator or map on H.

Gödel’s ontological argument is a theorem of quantified modal logic S5 with the non-logical predicate Pos for positivity and the defining condition

G(x) := ∀P [Pos(P) → P(x)]

together with the modal bridge axioms

* Pos(P) → □Pos(P),
* Pos(P) → Pos(□P),
* Existence is positive,
* etc.

and the S5 principles. Its validity is read off in Kripke semantics for S5: a set of possible worlds W with an equivalence accessibility relation R, a valuation V, and the clauses

w ⊩ □φ iff ∀v [wRv → v ⊩ φ].

That apparatus is set-theoretic meta-mathematics for modal logic. It is not part of the operator-algebraic formalism that defines observables and states. The □ operator has no canonical representation as a bounded or unbounded operator on H, nor as an element of a C*-algebra, and the worlds of a Kripke frame are not vectors, rays or projection lattices in the quantum formalism. Adding a Kripke frame to a C*-algebraic model breaks the * -representation, the spectral theorem and the probabilistic interpretation that define the customary setting.

The orthomodular lattice L(H) of closed subspaces / projections is the physically intended propositional calculus. It is non-distributive and non-Boolean. The classical closure conditions on positive properties that Gödel uses, and the unrestricted conjunction of incompatible properties needed for a single object to possess all positive properties at once, are not valid in L(H). Necessitation and the Barcan rules that drive the S5 derivation have no natural state-functional semantics on that lattice.

It is true, as colleagues 1,10,2 note, that S5 and Gödel’s axioms can be coded up in ZFC, and therefore in the set-theoretic background in which Hilbert spaces are defined. That is a formalisability statement in the metalanguage, not a theorem of the Hilbert-space / operator-algebra mathematics used for physical predictions. The conclusion ∃x G(x) is existence relative to the imported metaphysical modal axioms and the S5 Kripke semantics, not a consequence of the spectral calculus, the Schrödinger equation or the Born rule.

In the physical, i.e. customary quantum-mechanical, sense the modal positivity axioms are not expressible, let alone provable, inside the formalism itself. The proof is therefore a conditional meta-mathematical one, not a proof of a God-like entity within the customary mathematics of quantum mechanics.

No, not as an internal/unconditional theorem of the mathematics that is actually used to formulate and compute quantum mechanics.

The mathematics that is customary for non-relativistic QM is classical mathematics: a separable complex Hilbert space H, self-adjoint observables, spectral measures, C*-/von Neumann algebras, Born rule, etc., developed in ZFC + analysis and reasoned about in classical first-order logic. In that meta-theory the propositional content that is intrinsic to the formalism is the orthomodular lattice L(H) of closed subspaces/projections, not a Boolean modal algebra.

Gödel’s ontological argument is a theorem of quantified modal S5 with a non-logical primitive Pos(P) and the axioms

Pos(P)→□Pos(P), Pos(P)→Pos(□P), ¬Pos(¬P), Pos(Ex), closure under conjunction/implication,
G(x)≡∀P[Pos(P)→P(x)]

from which S5+PosAx ⊢ □∃x G(x) and ⊢∃x G(x). 
ZFC is strong enough to code syntax, Kripke frames and S5, so the derivation can be transcribed in the set-theoretic meta-language in which H, B(H) and spectral theory are defined. That is a formalisability/consistency-relative statement only.

□,◇, Pos in Gödel’s metaphysical sense, essence and necessary existence are not part of the Hilbert-space/operator-algebraic object language. They have no canonical interpretation as bounded/unbounded operators on H, as maps on L(H), or as elements of a C*-algebra, and they are not theorems of functional analysis, spectral calculus, Stone–von Neumann, CCR or the Born rule. Positivity in the physical sense is A≥0, not metaphysical positivity of properties.

On the physically intended internal reading the obstruction is stronger. L(H) is orthomodular, non-distributive and non-Boolean, with no canonical S5 necessity operator. The classical closure of positive properties under conjunction/implication and the unrestricted S5 necessitation/iteration used by Gödel are not validated in L(H); Kochen–Specker type incompatibility blocks a single entity possessing all positive properties at once in the quantum-logical semantics. Imposing S5 externally breaks the *-representation and spectral interpretation.

Hence at most one obtains the familiar conditional meta-mathematical fact: if Gödel’s S5 positivity axioms are postulated as extra-physical premises, their consistency can be expressed in the ZFC meta-theory shared with QM and the formal consequence ∃x G(x) follows in that meta-theory. It is not a theorem of the customary Hilbert-space/C*-algebraic mathematics of QM, and it is not a physical existence statement about a state, ray or observable. In the physics sense the existence of a Gödelian god-like entity is not provable from the customary mathematics of quantum mechanics.

The native propositions are elements of the orthomodular lattice ${\cal L}(H)$ of closed subspaces/projections. Kripke semantics for S5 is a set-theoretic meta-object: a frame $\langle W,R\rangle$ with $R$ an equivalence relation, a valuation $V$, and the clause $w\Vdash\Box\phi$ iff $\phi$ holds at all $v$ with $wRv$. $W,R,V$ are sets in the metalanguage in which $H$ is defined. That is why the derivation

${\rm PosAx}+S5\vdash\exists x\,G(x),\; G(x)\equiv\forall P[Pos(P)\to P(x)]$

Positivity in the physical sense is $A\ge0$ in spectral order, not Gödel’s metaphysical positivity, and necessity is not an observable.

${\rm Pos}(P)\to{\rm Pos}(\Box P)$,

classical functional analysis.  $H$ is a separable complex Hilbert space,
observables are self-adjoint operators, states are rays/density operators,
measurement is spectral theory, and the formalism is developed in
ZFC+analysis with classical first-order logic in the meta-theory. The native
physical propositional content is the orthomodular lattice ${\cal L}(H)$ of
closed subspaces/projections.

$Pos(P)$, $\Box,\Diamond$, essence and necessary existence are not primitives
of that object language.  They have no canonical realisation as bounded or
unbounded operators on $H$, as elements of $B(H)$ or $C^{*}$/von Neumann
algebras, or as structure preserving maps on ${\cal L}(H)$.  Positivity in
physics is spectral positivity $A\ge0$, not Gödel’s metaphysical $Pos$, and
necessity is not an observable.  The Gödel definition

$G(x)\equiv\forall P[Pos(P)\to P(x)]$

together with

$Pos(P)\to\Box Pos(P),\;Pos(P)\to Pos(\Box P),\;Pos(E),$
closure of $Pos$ under $\wedge,\to$, $\neg Pos(\neg P)$, etc.,

and S5 necessitation/Barcan is a quantified modal theorem.  From
$S5+PosAx$ one gets $\vdash\Box\exists xG(x)$ and $\vdash\exists xG(x)$.  That
derivation is purely modal-metaphysical.

ZFC is indeed strong enough to code syntax, Kripke frames and quantified S5,
so the $S5+PosAx$ derivation can be transcribed in the set-theoretic
meta-language in which $H$, $B(H)$ and the spectral theorem are defined.
That is a formalisability/consistency-relative statement:

$ S5+PosAx\vdash\exists x G(x) $

is expressible in the classical ZFC background shared with QM.  It is
existence in a model of the imported modal positivity axioms, not a theorem
of the Hilbert-space/operator-algebraic language itself and it has no
operational content in states, observables and the Born rule.

On the physically intended internal reading the obstruction is real.  ${\cal
L}(H)$ is non-Boolean, non-distributive and has no canonical S5 necessity
operator.  The classical distributive closure of positive properties and the
unrestricted S5 necessitation/Barcan steps used essentially in Gödel’s proof
are not validated by the state-functional semantics on ${\cal L}(H)$; 
$\Box$ has no structure-preserving interpretation on $H$ or ${\cal L}(H)$,
and Kochen–Specker type incompatibility blocks the simultaneous possession of
all positive properties required for $G$.

Hence there is no unconditional, physically meaningful theorem $\exists x
G(x)$ of the customary Hilbert-space/$C^{*}$-algebraic mathematics used for
quantum mechanics, and no existence statement about an entity in $H$ or in the
algebra of observables follows from states, observables and the Born rule.
At most one has the familiar conditional meta-mathematical fact that, if
Gödel’s S5 positivity axioms are postulated as extra-physical premises, they
can be formalised in the classical ZFC meta-theory that underlies QM and the
conditional existence result follows there.  In the physics sense the proof is
ungrounded.

I want to sharpen the intrinsic vs meta distinction that several of us have already been pointing to, because it is where the Kripke semantics point lives.

The mathematics that is actually customary for non-relativistic quantum mechanics is the object language of functional analysis: a separable complex Hilbert space H, self-adjoint observables with spectral measures, states as rays/density operators, B(H) or C*/von Neumann algebras, Born rule, all developed in ZFC+analysis and reasoned about in classical first-order logic. The native physical propositional structure is the orthomodular lattice L(H) of closed subspaces/projections.

That language contains vectors, inner products, operators, spectra and probabilities. It contains no primitive □/◇, no metaphysical predicate Pos(P), no notion of essence or necessary existence, and no Kripke accessibility relation built into H, B(H) or L(H).

Gödel’s derivation is 
G(x) := ∀P[Pos(P)→P(x)]
with PosAx 
Pos(P)→□Pos(P), Pos(P)→Pos(□P), Pos(E), closure under ∧,→, etc.,
and S5. Soundness is read in Kripke semantics, i.e. a set-theoretic frame ⟨W,R⟩ with R an equivalence relation and w ⊩ □φ iff φ holds at all v with wRv. W,R,V are set-theoretic meta-objects in the background in which H is defined. 

It is true, and trivial, that ZFC is strong enough to code syntax, Kripke frames and S5, so the whole S5+PosAx derivation can be transcribed in the same set-theoretic meta-language that underlies H and the spectral theorem. That is a formalisability/consistency statement: “if S5+PosAx are assumed, ZFC proves ∃x G(x)”. It is not a theorem of the Hilbert-space/operator-algebraic language itself and it gives no operational content in terms of states, observables and probabilities.

The physically intended obstruction is sharper. □ has no canonical interpretation as a bounded/unbounded operator on H, as an element of B(H), or as a structure-preserving map on L(H). “Possible world” is not a ray, density operator or state on a C*-algebra. Positivity in physics is spectral positivity A≥0, not Gödel metaphysical Pos(P), and necessity is not an observable.

Moreover L(H) is non-Boolean and non-distributive and has no canonical S5 necessity operator. The classical distributive closure of positive properties and the unrestricted S5 necessitation/Barcan steps used essentially in Gödel’s proof are not validated by the state-functional semantics on L(H); incompatible properties cannot be simultaneously possessed in the quantum-logical semantics. Imposing S5 externally breaks the *-representation and spectral interpretation that define the customary setting.

Hence there is no unconditional, physically meaningful theorem ∃x G(x) of the customary Hilbert-space/C*-algebraic mathematics used for quantum mechanics, and a fortiori no proof of the existence of a Gödelian god-like entity from states, observables and the Born rule. At most we have the familiar conditional meta-mathematical fact that the S5+PosAx derivation can be encoded in the classical set-theoretic background shared with QM. The existence proved is existence in a model of the imported modal-metaphysical axioms, not existence in H or in the algebra of observables. In the physics sense the argument is ungrounded, and Kripke semantics remains meta-logic, not part of the customary QM object language.

The mathematics that is actually customary for non-relativistic quantum mechanics is the object language of physics: a separable complex Hilbert space H, self-adjoint observables with spectral measures, states as rays/density operators, B(H) and C*/von Neumann algebras, the Born rule. It is developed in ZFC+analysis and reasoned about in classical first-order logic in the meta-theory. The native physical propositional structure is the orthomodular lattice L(H) of closed subspaces/projections.

That language contains vectors, inner products, operators, spectra and probabilities. It contains no primitive □,◇, no primitive metaphysical predicate Pos(P) in Gödel’s sense, no notion of essence or necessary existence, and no Kripke accessibility relation built into H, B(H) or L(H).

Gödel’s argument is

G(x) ≡ ∀P[Pos(P)→P(x)]

with PosAx

Pos(P)→□Pos(P), Pos(P)→Pos(□P), Pos(E), closure of Pos under ∧,→, ¬Pos(¬P), etc.,

and S5. From S5+PosAx one gets ⊢ □∃x G(x) and ⊢ ∃x G(x). That is a theorem of quantified modal logic, and its usual soundness is read off Kripke semantics for S5: a frame ⟨W,R⟩ with R an equivalence relation and w ⊩ □φ iff φ holds at all v with wRv.

A Kripke frame and the clause for □ are set-theoretic meta-semantics for modal logic. W,R,V are sets in the metalanguage in which H is defined. □ has no canonical interpretation as a bounded or unbounded operator on H, nor as a structure-preserving map on L(H). “Possible world” is not a ray, density operator or state on a C*-algebra. Positivity in physics is spectral positivity A ≥0, not Gödel metaphysical positivity, and necessity is not an observable.

It is true that ZFC is strong enough to code syntax, Kripke frames and S5, so the S5+PosAx derivation can be transcribed in the set-theoretic background that also defines H and B(H). That is a formalisability/consistency-relative observation in the classical meta-theory shared with QM: if S5+PosAx are postulated as extra-physical premises, they can be written down in ZFC and the conditional consequence ∃x G(x) follows there.

It is not a theorem of the Hilbert-space/operator-algebraic object language itself and it has no operational content in states, observables and the Born rule. On the physically intended internal reading the obstruction is sharper: L(H) is orthomodular, non-Boolean and non-distributive. It has no canonical S5 necessity operator. The classical distributive closure of positive properties and the unrestricted S5 necessitation/Barcan steps used essentially in Gödel’s proof are not validated by the state-functional semantics on L(H); incompatible properties cannot be simultaneously possessed, and □ has no structure-preserving realisation in L(H). Imposing S5 externally breaks the *-representation and spectral interpretation that define the customary setting.

Hence there is no unconditional, physically meaningful theorem ∃x G(x) of the customary Hilbert-space/C*-algebraic mathematics used for quantum mechanics, and no existence statement about an entity in H or in the algebra of observables follows from quantum theory. At most one obtains the familiar conditional meta-mathematical fact that, assuming Gödel’s modal positivity axioms as imported metaphysical premises, the existence claim is a theorem of the classical set theory in which quantum mechanics is formulated. In the physics sense, internal to the customary formalism, the Gödelian god-like entity is not provable, and the proof is ungrounded without importing an external modal-metaphysical apparatus.
